title: Sorted bulk RNA-seq profiling of human peripheral blood mononuclear cell populations across diverse in vitro immune stimuli
description: Human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy, de-identified donors were stimulated in vitro with a subset of immune stimuli and profiled by bulk RNA sequencing following fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS). Following a 48-hour assay, major immune cell populations were isolated, including monocytes, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and B cells, and subjected to RNA-seq. This dataset captures cell type-specific transcriptional responses to B cell stimulator cells (BCS), CytoStim™, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and IFN-α, alongside unstimulated baseline controls. Overall design: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells isolated from 6 healthy human donors were exposed in vitro for 48 hours to B cell stimulator cells (BCS), CytoStim™, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), IFN-α, or unstimulated baseline control conditions. Following stimulation, major immune cell populations were isolated by FACS on a BD FACSAria™ Fusion using lineage markers for monocytes (CD14+), CD4+ T cells (CD3+, CD4+), CD8+ T cells (CD3+, CD8+), and B cells (CD19+, CD20+). RNA was extracted from sorted cells and transcriptomes measured by bulk RNA-seq.
